provenance: Reference data for Feature Kickoff, not example data: the compliance frameworks a person can approve for a feature, and the third-party providers offered as quick picks. Triggers are the words that make the rule-based suggester propose a framework; a suggestion is only ever a proposal until a named person approves the selection. Obligations are the short list the analysis plans work against. Change this file by pull request, reviewed by the architecture owner.

compliance.name: PSD2 and the RTS on strong customer authentication
compliance.summary: EU rules for payment services: strong customer authentication, consent for account access, and a dedicated interface for third-party providers.
obligations: Strong customer authentication on account access and payment initiation, with any RTS exemption stated
Explicit, revocable consent for account access; re-authentication at least every 180 days for AIS
Dedicated TPP interface with fallback, and availability and performance reporting
Operational and security incident reporting to the competent authority

compliance.name: Berlin Group NextGenPSD2
compliance.summary: The API standard most EU banks use to meet PSD2: consent resources, SCA approaches and TPP identification.
obligations: Consent resource for account access
SCA approach declared: redirect, decoupled or embedded
TPP identified by an eIDAS certificate (QWAC)

compliance.name: UK Open Banking Standard (Read/Write API)
compliance.summary: The UK standard for account information and payment initiation APIs, with its security profile and conformance tooling.
obligations: Account access consent resource with permissions scoped per data cluster
FAPI security profile: mTLS and signed request objects
Dynamic Client Registration for TPP onboarding
Functional, security and DCR conformance runs as their own piece of work

compliance.name: CFPB Personal Financial Data Rights (Section 1033)
compliance.summary: The US rule giving consumers the right to share their financial data with authorized third parties. Its compliance dates and scope have been under reconsideration: confirm the current status with Legal before planning against it.
obligations: Confirm the rule's current status and dates with Legal before committing scope
Developer interface in a qualified industry standard format (for example FDX)
Authorization disclosures and consumer revocation of third-party access
Data minimisation and retention limits for authorized third parties

compliance.name: FDX API (Financial Data Exchange)
compliance.summary: The North American data-sharing API standard aggregators and data access networks build on.
obligations: Endpoints and payloads mapped to the FDX version the partner certifies against
Consent and token lifecycle per the FDX security model
Membership access to the full specification confirmed

compliance.name: GDPR / UK GDPR
compliance.summary: Rules for processing personal data of people in the EU and UK: lawful basis, minimisation, data subject rights and processor contracts.
obligations: Lawful basis recorded per purpose; consent captured where it is the basis
Data minimisation and retention periods for every new field
DPIA for high-risk processing
Data subject rights: access, erasure and portability cover the new data
Processor agreements with every third party receiving personal data

compliance.name: PCI DSS v4.0.1
compliance.summary: The card industry's security standard for anyone storing, processing or transmitting cardholder data.
obligations: Keep PAN out of scope where possible (tokenisation, hosted fields)
No storage of sensitive authentication data after authorisation
Segmentation and access control for the cardholder data environment
Assessment scope updated for the new flow

compliance.name: EU DORA (Digital Operational Resilience Act)
compliance.summary: EU requirements for ICT risk management, incident reporting, resilience testing and ICT third-party providers.
obligations: New ICT third-party provider entered in the register of information
Contract carries the provisions DORA Art. 30 requires
Incident classification and reporting cover the new service
Resilience testing includes the new dependency and its exit plan

compliance.name: ISO 20022 payment messages
compliance.summary: The message standard behind SEPA, SWIFT CBPR+, FedNow and most instant payment schemes.
obligations: Message mapping to pain, pacs and camt with field-level rules
Structured remittance and address data where the scheme requires it
Status reports (pacs.002) mapped to the status the customer sees

compliance.name: AML / KYC (AMLD, BSA)
compliance.summary: Customer due diligence, sanctions screening and transaction monitoring obligations.
obligations: Customer due diligence and identity verification before the product is usable
Sanctions and PEP screening, with rescreening
Transaction monitoring rules cover the new flow
Records kept for the retention period

compliance.name: GLBA Privacy and Safeguards Rules
compliance.summary: US rules for how financial institutions disclose, share and protect customers' nonpublic personal information.
obligations: Privacy notice covers the new data use and sharing
Safeguards: access control, encryption in transit and at rest
Oversight of service providers that receive customer information

compliance.name: CCPA / CPRA (California)
compliance.summary: California consumer privacy rights: notice, access, deletion, correction and opt-out of sale or sharing.
obligations: Notice at collection for any new data
Right to know, delete, correct and opt out cover the new data
Service provider contracts for vendors receiving the data

compliance.name: Nacha Operating Rules (ACH)
compliance.summary: The rules governing ACH payments in the US, including account validation and authorization.
obligations: Account validation for first-use WEB debits
Authorization and return handling per SEC code
Account numbers protected at rest

compliance.name: FAPI 2.0 Security Profile
compliance.summary: The OpenID Foundation's high-security OAuth profile for financial APIs.
obligations: Sender-constrained tokens (mTLS or DPoP)
Pushed authorization requests and PKCE
Client authentication by private_key_jwt or mTLS

compliance.name: OWASP API Security Top 10 / ASVS
compliance.summary: The baseline security review for any new or changed API: authorization, authentication, resource limits.
obligations: Object-level authorization checked on every endpoint
Authentication and token handling reviewed
Rate limiting and resource consumption limits
Threat model for any new trust boundary

compliance.name: WCAG 2.2 AA / European Accessibility Act
compliance.summary: Accessibility requirements for customer-facing web and mobile journeys.
obligations: Keyboard and screen reader paths through every new screen
Contrast, focus visibility and target sizes per WCAG 2.2 AA
Accessibility checks in the definition of done

compliance.name: SOC 2 vendor assurance
compliance.summary: Reviewing each new vendor's SOC 2 Type II report and the controls it expects of us.
obligations: Current SOC 2 Type II report from each new vendor reviewed
Complementary user entity controls implemented on our side

providers.name: Salt Edge
providers.summary: Account information and payment initiation connectivity, with data enrichment.

providers.name: Ninth Wave
providers.summary: Open finance data connectivity for US financial institutions. Its API docs are shared with customers; paste the docs link you were given.

providers.name: Plaid
providers.summary: Account linking, balances, transactions, identity and payments.

providers.name: Akoya
providers.summary: An FDX-based data access network between institutions and data recipients.

providers.name: Yapily
providers.summary: Open banking data and payments infrastructure.
